rationale: This sample is a tiny (2KB text, 4 functions), pointer-heavy linked-list micro-benchmark whose work runs inside main's hot iteration loop, so the table favors low-overhead structural passes over expensive dataflow inflation. SUB is weighted strongly (negligible runtime/size cost, broad static-analysis resistance across the arithmetic in list indexing and length counting), and FLA is kept moderately high as the main resilience anchor since flattening main disrupts the loop-structure recognition an analyst would rely on, but its RuntimeCost weight is held to 0.5 to keep the dispatch overhead in the hot loop acceptable. SPLIT, IBR, ICALL, and IGV are included at moderate levels to add control-flow, branch-target, call-site, and global-access diversity cheaply — with ICALL tempered because the program has very few call sites (mostly iostream I/O) and IBR tempered because indirect branches in the pointer-chasing inner loops carry both runtime and correctness exposure. BCF is omitted entirely: its substantial code-size and runtime inflation is a poor trade on a 2KB binary with a single dominant hot function, where it would balloon text and slow the measured benchmark while adding little beyond what FLA+IBR already provide. All CorrectnessRisk weights stay low-to-moderate since cost dimensions are treated as penalty sensitivities — the selector should avoid applying a pass where its cost/risk features are high for a given function — preserving correctness for this benchmark-driven sample.
